text:
matt: heads up — canary p99 jumped from ~120ms to ~240ms around 1869994200 after the merge of a couple of runtime changes (PRs 4123 + 4150). noticing it on the kv-heavy workload.
julia: ugh. which runtime changes specifically? kernel selector or batching heuristics?
alejandro: 4123 touched kernel selection thresholds, 4150 changed batching prefetch behavior. could be interaction.
matt: deploy-bot posted the canary failure earlier: 
```
[deploy-bot] canary: p99 240ms (baseline 120ms) — triggered alert, rolling back paused
```
ci-bot: perf-smoke job shows the same trend on our nightly perf matrix, reproduces on x86-gpu-small.
sam: I tried a local run with HEAD and a pinned old kernel, and saw p99 back to normal. suggests kernel selector flip? :eyes:
julia: can we get a small repro harness for the kv workload and run git bisection with the perf-run command? I can try to isolate if kernel selection is the changelist.
alejandro: plan: (1) reproduce locally with the exact perf-smoke config; (2) run git bisection building artifacts; (3) if bisection points to selector config, do a quick revert candidate.
grace: throwing ideas — also check the KV cache hit-rate and prefix caching logs. batching prefetch could cause different sequence lengths and make the kernel selector pick a slower path.
matt: logging from the canary: 
```
2026-03-15T10:12:03Z runtime: kernel=opt-kernel-v2 seq_mean=256 seq_p99=1024 batch_size=6 kv_hits=0.82 p99_ms=238
```
matt: older canary before merges: 
```
2026-03-12T09:08:11Z runtime: kernel=opt-kernel-v1 seq_mean=128 seq_p99=512 batch_size=4 kv_hits=0.86 p99_ms=118
```
julia: interesting — kernel changed from v1->v2 and batch_size bumped. maybe the selector threshold formula got stricter and chooses v2 (which is regressing on long sequences).
sam: I can reproduce the p99 locally ~80% of runs. it's flaky. my hunch: a timing window where prefetch increases token churn which breaks batching alignment and falls back to a slower kernel path.
alejandro: to run git bisection we need a reliable script that boots the perf harness and returns pass/fail automatically. I can wire one up; want to use the same smoke profile as CI.
julia: please add an env toggle so we can force the kernel selector to old thresholds for testing: e.g., RUNTIME_KERNEL_SELECTOR=legacy
matt: quick bisect command I used locally: 
```bash
git bisect start --term-old=GOOD --term-new=BAD
# build script returns 0 for good, 1 for bad
GIT_BUILD_SCRIPT=./tools/build-and-run-smoke.sh git bisect run ./tools/check-p99.sh
```
sam: check-p99.sh will need to run the harness long enough; set ITER=200 to avoid flakes.
ci-bot: note — perf-smoke job runtime is 8 minutes; gating bisection on CI will be slow.
grace: alternative: narrow to the subset of commits touching kernel selector config and batching prefetch files then bisect that range first.
alejandro: good idea. I already grep'd and produced a short candidate set: commits from d1a2..f3b4 (7 commits). I'll start local bisect on that range.
matt: if bisection points to kernel selector commit, we should revert as rollout-blocker for canary and run a controlled canary with the revert.
julia: I can prepare the revert PR and hold it as ready-to-merge if bisect confirms.
sam: logs from a local failing run attached to thread (pasted): 
```
[run] seq 1024: kernel-switcher: selected opt-kernel-v2 (cost_estimate=1.12)
[run] batching: aligned batches=3 misaligned=2 prefetch=1
[run] p99=242ms
```
sam: and a succeeding run where I force legacy selector: 
```
[run] kernel-switcher: selected opt-kernel-v1 (cost_estimate=0.95)
[run] batching: aligned batches=5 misaligned=0 prefetch=0
[run] p99=115ms
```
julia: good signal. alejandro — can you run perf traces on both runs and upload flamegraphs? we want to see if opt-kernel-v2 has a hotspot in attention kernels.
alejandro: will do. kicking off two runs now (good vs bad). attaching flamegraphs when done.
ci-bot: perf-artifact: /artifacts/1869994321/trace-good.svg and /artifacts/1869994321/trace-bad.svg
matt: I skimmed the bad trace — attention matmul kernel has a 2.6x higher time slice in v2 path compared to v1.
grace: that supports kernel-level regression. could be a kernel parameter change or a missing tiling fallback.
julia: action items: 
- alejandro: finish perf traces + diff and post before EOD (ts 1869994680)
- sam: continue bisect runs and mark the first commit that flips perf
- matt: queue revert PR template (if confirmed) and hold for review
- grace: prepare canary hold instructions for SRE
matt: also add a short toil script to run the harness in a deterministic seed to reduce flakiness: ./tools/run-smoke.sh --seed=42
sam: noted. I'll run the deterministic bisect next.
julia: thanks all. please post any new logs here. tagging @sre on the canary hold if we need to pause further rollouts. :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: canary paused for manual review per request by matt.
